title: Python break Statement
learningObjectives: Explain the purpose and behavior of python break statement.
Write syntactically correct loop code using appropriate indentation.
Trace loop execution for representative inputs.
Select a suitable loop-control statement for a task.
Apply iteration to a practical collection or counting problem.

understand.concept: The break statement immediately terminates the nearest enclosing loop. Execution continues with the first statement after that loop. In nested loops, break exits only the innermost loop in which it appears.
understand.whyItMatters: break is useful when a search finds its target or a task reaches a condition that makes further iterations unnecessary.
understand.analogy: It is like stopping a search as soon as the required item is found.
understand.analogyLimit: break changes normal loop flow; use it deliberately and keep the exit condition understandable.

explain.narrative:
## 1. Exit a loop early

Place `break` inside a loop when a condition means no further iterations are needed.

## 2. Continue after the loop

After break, Python executes the statement following the loop.

## 3. Nested loops

A break exits only the nearest enclosing loop. An outer loop may continue.

examples.title: Stop at a target number
examples.explanation: When number becomes three, break exits the loop before printing it.

examples.title: Find a matching word
examples.explanation: The loop stops as soon as the target is found.

examples.title: Break a while loop
examples.explanation: The explicit break ends the otherwise unbounded loop when attempts reaches two.

examples.title: Break only the inner loop
examples.explanation: Each break exits the inner column loop, then the outer row loop continues.

examples.title: Stop processing at a sentinel
examples.explanation: The negative sentinel ends iteration before later values are processed.

practise.guidedTask: Search a list for a target value and use break to stop after the first match.
practise.independentTask: Process a sequence of values until a sentinel is reached. Print only values before the sentinel and report that processing stopped.
hints: Put break inside the loop body.

practise.challenge: Write nested loops where an inner break occurs and trace why the outer loop continues. Then design an explicit strategy to exit both loops if required.

questions.explanation: break terminates the closest loop containing it.

questions.prompt: What executes after a break exits a loop?
options: The next statement after the loop
questions.answer: The next statement after the loop
questions.explanation: Normal execution continues after the terminated loop.

questions.prompt: In nested loops, which loop does break exit?
questions.explanation: break applies to the nearest enclosing loop.

questions.prompt: Which is a common use for break?
options: Stop a search after finding the target
questions.answer: Stop a search after finding the target
questions.explanation: Further search is unnecessary after the target is found.

questions.prompt: Does break skip only one iteration?
questions.explanation: continue skips an iteration; break exits the loop.
